title: Todos los días lo mismo
blurbEn: A routine that went on for years, and the single afternoon that broke it. Habits in one tense, the turning point in the other.
body:
Antes mi vida era muy tranquila y siempre igual.

Me levantaba a las siete, desayunaba café con tostadas y salía de casa a las ocho. Trabajaba hasta las seis, volvía a casa, cenaba y leía un rato antes de dormir.

Todos los días lo mismo. No era una vida mala, pero era un poco aburrida.

Un día de octubre decidí cambiar algo. Busqué clases de español por internet y me apunté a un curso.

Aquella tarde no leí un libro. Escribí mi primera frase en español: «Me llamo Ana y quiero aprender».
translationEn:
Before, my life was very quiet and always the same.

I got up at seven, had coffee and toast for breakfast and left home at eight. I worked until six, came home, had dinner and read for a while before sleeping.

Every day the same. It was not a bad life, but it was a little boring.

One day in October I decided to change something. I looked for Spanish classes on the internet and signed up for a course.

That afternoon I did not read a book. I wrote my first sentence in Spanish: "My name is Ana and I want to learn."

Me levantaba.note: Not one morning — every morning, for years. English hides this behind a plain 'I got up'.

decidí.note: The tense switches here, and the switch is the whole point: one October day, once. That is what ends the routine.

Aquella.note: 'aquel' points further away than 'ese' — that one, back then.

phrases.gloss: One day in October I decided
phrases.note: 'Un día' plus the preterite. A single point in time, breaking a run of habits.
